PANOORIN | Kinumpirma ng Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP) ang kumakalat na video sa social media na nagpapakita ng pagnanakaw ng ilang firefighters volunteers sa nasunog na supermarket sa Barangay Pasong Putik, Fairview, Quezon City.

Sa panayam ng media sa Camp Crame, sinabi ni BFP Spokesperson Fire Supt. Anthony Arroyo na ang kumakalat na video sa social media ay nangyari habang nagsasagawa ng firefighting operation at mapping operation ang mga bumbero.

Sa naturang video, kumaha raw ng mga gamit partikular na ng mga alak ang ilang firefighter volunteers. | via Diane Lear

data.text:
More than two years since they convened to develop initial short-term measures to address the perennial problem of overcrowded jails and prisons in the country, justice system stakeholders are now shifting their focus to long-term reforms with the launch of the Second National Decongestion Summit on January 21, 2026, at the Manila Hotel.

Chief Justice Alexander G. Gesmundo said the gathering, organized by the Justice Sector Coordinating Council (JSCC), serves as a platform to build on the numerous achievements of the first Summit conducted in 2023.

The JSCC is a coordinative body composed of the #SupremeCourtPH (SC), the Department of Justice (DOJ), and the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG). 

Chief Justice Gesmundo highlighted key reforms under the Strategic Plan for Judicial Innovations 2022-2027,  disclosing that the SC En Banc is now deliberating the inclusion of a provision on custodial hearings in the proposed revisions of the Rules of Criminal Procedure. 

He also discussed other reforms which contributed to positive results, with data from the Bureau of Jail Management and Penology showing that the national jail congestion rate was reduced by 10% in just four months. 

Despite encouraging outcomes, the Chief Justice emphasized that the SC still recognizes the need for all branches of the government to do more.
